declared_proposition: Let A_2(X) and pi_2(X) be the odd prime-power-pair and twin-prime counts of TICKET-246, put Y=X+2, K=floor(log_2 Y), and let pi_odd(t) count odd primes at most t. If N_odd(Y) counts odd composite prime powers at most Y, then exactly N_odd(Y)=sum_(k=2)^K pi_odd(floor(Y^(1/k))). Consequently 0<=A_2(X)-pi_2(X)<=2N_odd(Y) <=2pi_odd(floor(sqrt(Y)))+2(K-2)pi_odd(floor(cuberoot(Y))). This strictly sharpens the exponent-blind TICKET-246 correction at every audited scale.
mathematical_argument: Every odd composite prime power has a unique representation p^k with odd prime p and k>=2, so counting by exponent gives the exact sum. As before, every false pair contains such a power in one of two coordinates, giving the factor-two union bound. The k=2 contribution is exactly pi_odd(floor sqrt(Y)); every one of the K-2 remaining contributions is at most the k=3 count, proving the sharper bound.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: The exact correction is smaller than the previous crude correction, but there is still no lower bound for A_2 exceeding it on unbounded scales. The finite sieve through ten million supplies no Type-II cancellation and no infinitude conclusion.

finite_computation_boundary: Prime-power and twin supports are enumerated through 10,000,000; the exact all-X count identity is combinatorial, but the finite rows imply no twin-prime infinitude.
logical_limit: The correction is now counted exactly and bounded more sharply, but no unbounded scale sequence has A_2 beyond that correction and no parity-breaking Type-II estimate is proved.

route_decision.discard: using the exponent-blind TICKET-246 O(sqrt(X) log(X)) correction as the final prime-power contamination scale
route_decision.retain: a scale-local nonperiodic Type-II lower bound for A_2 exceeding the exact odd composite-prime-power correction

claim_boundary: No twin-prime proof or counterexample; one exact contamination count formula and sharper sufficient target.
